item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani will make his return to the lineup tonight (Wednesday, September 23) against the San Diego Padres. The Dodgers have activated the two-way standout from the 15-day injured list after he took time to rest his nagging knee and biceps injuries. Ohtani will serve as the designated hitter for the remainder of the regular season and playoffs, as he is currently unable to pitch.
Ohtani's return comes at a crucial time for the Dodgers, who are looking to solidify their position in the National League West. According to MLB.com, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts confirmed that Ohtani is now in a better physical state, rating him an "eight or a nine" on a scale of one to ten. Ohtani has been progressing well in his hitting, having taken 30-40 swings off a Trajekt machine, which simulates real pitchers.
Despite his recent struggles at the plate, Ohtani remains a key player for the Dodgers. Before his injuries, he recorded a .902 OPS and hit a team-leading 30 home runs. In his last 24 games before going on the injured list, Ohtani hit .198 with 34 strikeouts. ABC7 reported that Roberts plans to play Ohtani in every remaining game to help him reacclimate to major league pitching.
The Dodgers have managed to maintain a strong record in Ohtani's absence, going 13-3 in the last 16 games. As they prepare for the playoffs, Ohtani's return as a designated hitter is expected to bolster their lineup. The Dodgers are also considering roster adjustments, with outfield prospect Josue De Paula potentially being sent down to make room for Ohtani.
For tonight's game, the Dodgers will face the Padres with right-handed pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto on the mound. The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and available on the MLB app.

item.title: [ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos] Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory
item.source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
item.dc:creator: ABC News; BETH HARRIS AP sports writer
item.description: Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month LOS ANGELES -- Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night in a series opener between rivals with the two best recor
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory
Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month
LOS ANGELES -- Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month.
The Dodgers (97-60) moved within one game of NL Central champion Milwaukee (98-59) for the top mark in the big leagues and home-field advantage throughout the postseason. However, the Brewers own the head-to-head tiebreaker.
Los Angeles needs one win or an Atlanta loss to clinch a first-round bye into a National League Division Series.
The NL West champion Dodgers improved to 15-5 in September with their fifth straight victory; the Padres fell to 14-5 and had their five-game winning streak snapped.
San Diego is tied with Chicago and Philadelphia at 87-70 for the three NL wild cards — four games ahead of Arizona with five to play.
Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado were a combined 1 for 7 with five strikeouts for the Padres.
The Dodgers chased Michael King (12-10) after four innings in his career-high 32nd start of the season. The right-hander gave up five runs on six hits and struck out five as his four-game winning streak ended.
Los Angeles broke out with four runs in the second. King got the first two outs on six pitches before loading the bases. Teoscar Hernández and rookie Josue De Paula hit consecutive singles before King plunked Andy Pages, who just came off the injured list.
King then issued back-to-back walks to Edman and Mookie Betts, forcing in two runs. Freddie Freeman's two-run single made it 4-0.
Betts had a ground-rule double and scored on Freeman's two-out single for a 5-0 lead in the fourth.
Edman's solo shot came with two outs in the sixth and Smith added a 396-foot drive with one out in the seventh for a 7-0 lead.
Brock Stewart started a bullpen game and Justin Wrobleski (12-5) got the win for the Dodgers, who used eight pitchers to earn the fifth shutout in franchise history when deploying at least that many.
Among them was reliever Edwin Díaz, who struck out two in one inning. Roki Sasaki's four-seam fastball touched 100 mph while he pitched one inning. The Japanese right-hander came off the injured list earlier Tuesday after missing nearly a month with a blister on his right middle finger.
Padres LHP Robbie Ray (13-8, 3.60 ERA) starts Wednesday against Dodgers RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51).
___
This story has been corrected to show the Dodgers scored six runs with two outs, not five.
___

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani to return from IL Wednesday, but Dodgers still have unanswered questions in final week
- Click here to listen to this article
-
The Dodgers have less than a week left of the regular season to round into playoff form. And their roster moves this series reflect that time crunch.
Manager Dave Roberts confirmed Tuesday afternoon that Shohei Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) was on track to be reinstated from the 15-day injured list on Wednesday. Ohtani is feeling “considerably” better than he was before the IL stint, according to Roberts.
“I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or a nine right now,” Roberts said before eight pitchers led the Dodgers’ 7-0 win against the San Diego Padres.
On Tuesday, they returned two other important postseason pieces, reinstating center fielder Andy Pages (fractured left hand) and right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) from the injured list.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliézer Alfonzo to triple-A Oklahoma City.
Sasaki took the fourth inning of the bullpen game and threw scoreless ball. He gave up a pair of singles, but his fastball had a little extra life in the short stint, averaging 98.7 mph and topping out at 101.7.
Pages went 0 for 2 but reached base twice, on a hit by pitch and a walk.
Even as players return, however, there are still questions the Dodgers have to answer in the last week of the season:
Where will Ohtani hit?
At least at first, Roberts plans to write Ohtani in at the top of the order, per usual. But shortstop Mookie Betts has entered the conversation.
“Certainly versus right-handed pitching [Ohtani] will be there,” Roberts said. “I do think I should think through the Mookie versus left situation, but I have to think about the entire lineup structure.”
Ohtani has hit leadoff in every game he’s started this year. But he hit No. 2 in 79 games the two previous seasons combined.
Even without Ohtani, the Dodgers lineup has been clicking. On Tuesday, Tommy Edman hit his second home run in as many games, and Will Smith homered for the third time in four days.
Is the rotation healthy?
Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, who exited his start last week with left groin tightness, threw a bullpen on Tuesday. He’s scheduled for one final regular-season start Saturday, Roberts said.
That means all four of the Dodgers’ projected playoff starters are lined up to pitch this Wednesday through Saturday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow on the mound for the last two games against the Padres, and Tarik Skubal and Snell in the first two games in San Francisco.
Who is the closer?
In short, it could change by the day.
“In a perfect world, as we all know the world’s not perfect, I would love [a set closer],” Roberts said. “I think if there’s an opportunity, for example, for Tanner [Scott] to pitch a high-leverage inning in the seventh or the eighth inning, it’s just hard to pass that up if he’s the best option right there. Because you just don’t know where the ninth inning is going to be.
“Those are things that you have to kind of toil with, and those are always good things for people to debate. Right now I don’t see a one-person closer.”
Sasaki stepped into that role last year. It’s unclear exactly how Roberts will use him this time around, but Roberts said he could be an option, depending on how he pitches coming off the IL.
“Last year it was one of those things where it was a situation of need, as far as where we were at with performance and health and guys,” Roberts said. “He filled that role admirably.”
Who gets the last bench spot?
The battle to serve as the left-handed bat off the bench in the postseason has come down to rookie Josue De Paula and injured catcher Dalton Rushing (right flexor strain). But with Rushing still on the IL, De Paula appears to have an edge.
Don’t read too much into the Dodgers’ corresponding move for Ohtani on Wednesday. If they option De Paula 10 days out from the first game of the National League Division Series, he can still be included on the roster.
The Dodgers will have to make another roster move later in the week, when they plan to activate Rushing. If they option a player to make room for Rushing, that player would only be eligible for the start of the NLDS as the corresponding transaction for an IL move.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers shutout of Padres reveals potential (and unexpected) playoff strength
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs. This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint. In their bid to three-peat as World Series champions, of course, the Dodgers are expected to be led by their star-studded rotation. item.content:encoded:
Last year, the Dodgers hardly used their bullpen in the playoffs.
This year, they would like that to once again be the blueprint.
In their bid to three-peat as World Series champions, of course, the Dodgers are expected to be led by their star-studded rotation. Shohei Ohtani isn’t pitching, but Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow are.
And if all goes according to plan, they will handle the bulk of the innings.
However, replicating the starting pitching excellence of last October won’t be easy. A season ago, the Dodgers’ four-man rotation of Ohtani, Yamamoto, Snell and Glasnow accounted for 113 of the team’s 165 postseason innings (including relief appearances from Glasnow and Yamamoto). Together, they posted a 2.55 ERA.
It was historic production.
Which also means, it’s fair to assume some regression will be possible –– both in workload and effectiveness.
Thus, having more reliable bullpen options this time around could be equally important for the Dodgers. And while that might have felt like a daunting reality earlier this year, when the unit was banged up and struggling through the middle portion of the campaign, Tuesday night was a reminder that the relief corps could be a strength in this fall’s title pursuit.
“Obviously we’ve had a lot of talent over the years,” manager Dave Roberts said. “But as far as sitting here today at the end of the season, it’s as good of shape as we’ve ever been in with the bullpen.”
In a 7-0 win over the San Diego Padres, the Dodgers were not supposed to have the pitching matchup –– countering Padres ace Michael King with a makeshift bullpen game in a rivalry series opener at Dodger Stadium.
Instead, eight different Dodgers relievers held the previous red-hot Padres to a five-hit shutout. Along the way, several arms who once seemed like question marks continued to round into increasingly promising form.
“It was fantastic,” Roberts said. “This is as good as our bullpen has been, has thrown.”
It started with opener Brock Stewart, a key right-handed weapon in the Dodgers’ bullpen who began the game with a scoreless first inning, continuing his late-season resurgence after another injury-plagued year.
From there, the baton was passed on down.
Justin Wrobleski, who is in the midst of a late-season conversion to the bullpen for the second-straight year, escaped a jam in the second. Blake Treinen, who might be on the postseason roster bubble given the Dodgers’ relief depth, offered one of his best outings of late by issuing only a two-out walk in a scoreless third.

The highlight of the night came in the fourth and fifth, when Roki Sasaki and Edwin Díaz hung a couple more zeroes in what were important appearances from each.
For Sasaki, the outing marked his first since returning from the injured list and making his own late-season move back to the bullpen, where he could reprise his role as closer from last year’s playoffs. He worked around a pair of singles with two strikeouts and a fastball that, even after being sidelined for the last month by a blister, sat at 99-100 mph.
For Díaz, Tuesday was not only a third-consecutive scoreless outing since his own return from the IL, but his most impressive yet as he makes a bid for the playoff roster. He retired the top of the Padres lineup in order with a pair of strikeouts, and has now retired 9 of 11 batters he has faced since rejoining the active roster.
Asked postgame if Díaz –– the $69 million offseason signing who lost the closer’s job amid a previously dismal debut Dodgers season –– could still pitch his way back into ninth-inning duties, Roberts said it’s “certainly possible.”
“The way he’s throwing, the ninth is possible, yes,” Roberts added.
By that point, the Dodgers had already pulled away from the Padres. They mounted a four-run rally with two outs in the second against King, who issued back-to-back bases-loaded walks to Tommy Edman and Mookie Betts before Freddie Freeman slashed a two-run single through the infield. The offense tacked on more runs in the fourth (on another Freeman RBI single), the sixth (on a solo home run from Tommy Edman), and the seventh (a Will Smith solo blast).
In what was the lineup’s toughest test in a while, they passed with flying colors.
Still, the night’s most encouraging developments came from the ‘pen, which capped off the game with two scoreless innings from Kyle Hurt, then stress-free appearances in the eighth and ninth from Alex Vesia and Jack Dreyer.
The unit’s most trusted arms at the moment, Tanner Scott (who figures to be vying with Sasaki for the postseason closer role) and Evan Phillips, weren’t even required. Nor was Edgardo Henriquez, who remains sidelined by a back injury but still could return in time for the playoffs.
“We know we have a good group, and anytime we get to carry the load and everybody has success and throws up zeros, it’s special,” Stewart said. “That’s really hard to do, for all eight guys or whatever it was today. So yeah, it’s cool.”
With a smirk, he added: “Write stories about it.”
Come October, of course, the Dodgers will be hoping their relievers are the main story.
But if the rotation falters, the club seems significantly better-suited to handle it than it did a year ago.
“That could change in a day, in a game, as we all know,” Roberts said. “But right now, feel really good about everyone out there.”

item.title: [truebluela.com] Dodgers notes: Blake Snell, Dalton Rushing, Will Klein
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — It’s the final week of the regular season and the Dodgers are sorting things out as they prepare for the postseason, which they hope will start on October 3 in the National League Division Series rather than September 29 in the wild card round. Before Tuesday’s game, Blake Snell pitched a bullpen session at Dodger Stadium as he works his way back from leaving last Wednesday’s start with left groin discomfort. Manager Dave Roberts said Snell is in line to start on Saturday in San Fr
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — It’s the final week of the regular season and the Dodgers are sorting things out as they prepare for the postseason, which they hope will start on October 3 in the National League Division Series rather than September 29 in the wild card round.
Before Tuesday’s game, Blake Snell pitched a bullpen session at Dodger Stadium as he works his way back from leaving last Wednesday’s start with left groin discomfort. Manager Dave Roberts said Snell is in line to start on Saturday in San Francisco against the Giants, with Tarik Skubal — currently on the bereavement list — starting Friday night at Oracle Park.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto starts Wednesday and Tyler Glasnow Thursday against the Padres.
Also on Tuesday, reliever Will Klein pitched a simulated inning against Dalton Rushing in a battle of players on the injured list. Klein is on the 60-day injured list with elbow discomfort and not eligible to be activated until September 30 at the earliest, but it looks like he’ll be in the stay-hot camp should the Dodgers have room to add him at some point later in the postseason, similar to in 2025 when Klein wasn’t active until the World Series and he pitched five scoreless innings, including four innings in the marathon Game 3.
“With Will it’s more get healthy, show that you’re healthy, throw to some hitters,” Roberts said. “He’ll throw during the week off, then we’ll kind of see if there’s an opportunity later on in the postseason, sort of like last year.”
Rushing is trying to work his way back from elbow discomfort suffered when practicing throwing. His role would be a left-handed bat off the bench, a role currently occupied by Josue De Paula, who has been the designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani out. But Ohtani is expected to be activated Wednesday barring an unforeseen setback.
That essentially sets up a battle between Rushing and De Paula for a postseason roster spot, though Roberts said the plan is to activate Rushing at some point this week to literally get back into the swing of things.
“Quality of at-bat, conducting an at-bat obviously, the ability to swing at strikes, take balls, get on base, get a hit. There’s potential slug with both guys. I think it’s a good debate,” Roberts said. “Hitting off the bench is very difficult so we’re trying to figure out who gives us the best chance.
“And to be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time he’s missed, and to think that you have [three] games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do. It’s not a knock on him, he’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, Given that we talk about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”
Activating both Ohtani and Rushing this week, when the Dodgers have 14 active position players, would require two corresponding moves to make room on the active roster. If De Paula doesn’t get sent down — “I think Josue has done a fantastic job,” Roberts said Tuesday — that might mean rough news for Alexes Call and Freeland, either this week or next.

item.title: [New York Post] Tyler Glasnow reveals ‘most likely’ usage plan for playoffs as Dodgers 3-peat quest kicks into gear
item.dc:creator: Valentina Martinez
item.description: The Dodgers have Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Blake Snell in the starting rotation. But where will Tyler Glasnow fit in the team’s postseason plans? “If it is the wild-card series, I probably wouldn’t start in one of those games. So, I’d probably be in the bullpen. And then the first series last year, we had four starters ,so I might be in that one,” Glasnow told Chris Rose. “So I think it’s just going to be like a all-hands-on-deck situation, which I prefer.” Glasnow played a versatile
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers have Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Blake Snell in the starting rotation.
But where will Tyler Glasnow fit in the team’s postseason plans?
“If it is the wild-card series, I probably wouldn’t start in one of those games. So, I’d probably be in the bullpen. And then the first series last year, we had four starters ,so I might be in that one,” Glasnow told Chris Rose.
“So I think it’s just going to be like a all-hands-on-deck situation, which I prefer.”
Glasnow played a versatile role for the Dodgers last October, sporting a 1.69 ERA in the postseason. He will likely be another multifaceted pitcher for the Dodgers in the playoffs.
Since his arrival to LA, the right-hander has never made it through a regular season without injury. While the 2026 season was no different, Glasnow is coming off a bounce-back start just before the regular season concludes.
The right-hander tossed six innings of two-run baseball with 10 strikeouts. It was a much improved performance from his previous start in Miami, where Glasnow allowed four earned runs in four innings.
With Shohei Ohtani’s absence in the rotation, Glasnow’s health is even more crucial heading into October. It appears the right-hander is feeling good and prepared to take on any role the Dodgers ask of him in the postseason.
“I think I feel relatively consistent. It’s just a matter of sometimes I’m not going to feel good, sometimes I will,” Glasnow said after his last start against the Giants.
“Today, I think it was a step in the right direction. I think it’s better than feeling really good for a long time before [the playoffs]. I’d rather kind of feel it, work through some stuff and have a good one right before [the] playoffs. So I think I’m in a good spot right now.”

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers manager squashes Blake Snell fears with latest update
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Blake Snell has been penciled back into the Dodgers’ rotation. Six days after Snell left an outing in Cincinnati after one inning with an initially concerning groin issue, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced on Tuesday that the two-time Cy Young Award winner is indeed expected to make one final regular-season start on Saturday in San Francisco. A major bullet, it appears, has been dodged. When Snell exited last week’s game against the Reds following just 19 pitches, it came as a potentially c
item.content:encoded:
Blake Snell has been penciled back into the Dodgers’ rotation.
Six days after Snell left an outing in Cincinnati after one inning with an initially concerning groin issue, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced on Tuesday that the two-time Cy Young Award winner is indeed expected to make one final regular-season start on Saturday in San Francisco.
A major bullet, it appears, has been dodged.
When Snell exited last week’s game against the Reds following just 19 pitches, it came as a potentially critical blow to the Dodgers’ rotation.
Three times in the previous five years, Snell has suffered groin injuries. Each time he missed at least 3-4 weeks — a timeline that would now have put his postseason availability in doubt.
However, Snell was optimistic from the start that this episode was not as severe as his past bouts with groin problems. He resumed catch play over the weekend and said his groin felt like an “8 out of 10.”
Snell took another step forward on Tuesday, throwing a bullpen session before the start of the Dodgers’ three-game series against the Padres. Roberts said Snell is expected to throw one more bullpen later this week before getting a final green light to make Saturday’s start.
The Dodgers considered shutting down Snell for the rest of the regular season to give him a couple extra weeks of rest before the start of the playoffs.
But that plan would have risked too long of a layoff for the 33-year-old left-hander. And the progress he has made in recent days was enough for the Dodgers to feel confident giving him one more start to prepare for October.
Barring any other unforeseen setbacks, the Dodgers should have their Big 4 starters — Snell, Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tyler Glasnow — all available to feature in their playoff rotation.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers' Blake Snell Making Return Just in Time for Postseason
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers starter Blake Snell will pitch against the San Francisco Giants on Saturday after tweaking his groin last week. Snell felt some tightness in his groin ahead of his last start against the Cincinnati Reds, but tried pitching through it. The injury raised some concerns about Snell’s postseason availability, as he struggled with similar injuries in 2021,
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers starter Blake Snell will pitch against the San Francisco Giants on Saturday after tweaking his groin last week.
Snell felt some tightness in his groin ahead of his last start against the Cincinnati Reds, but tried pitching through it. He only lasted one inning in the outing, pulling himself out of the game after the first inning to make way for Blake Treinen.
The injury raised some concerns about Snell’s postseason availability, as he struggled with similar injuries in 2021, 2022 and 2024, but his return bodes well for his involvement in the Dodgers’ postseason.
How Has Snell Performed This Season?
Snell only has eight appearances with the Dodgers under his belt so far this season, pitching 38.2 innings while striking out 52 batters while posting a 1.86 ERA.
He didn’t make an appearance until May after spending the first month or so of the season on the injured list with fatigue in his shoulder, but immediately went back on the injured list after allowing five runs in three innings with loose bodies in his elbow.
The left-hander came back into the rotation in August, and immediately looked his best upon his return. He allowed just three earned runs and struck out 31 batters through his four starts after coming off of the injured list, spanning 23 innings pitched.
In September, Snell has thrown 12.2 innings while allowing just one earned run and striking out 16 batters.
What Role Will Snell Have in October?
Snell, without a doubt, will have a spot as a starter in the Dodgers’ rotation come the postseason, likely joined by Tyler Glasnow, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal.
Despite his limited game time this year, Snell has proven himself as a key pitcher for the Dodgers, and also performed well during last year’s postseason. He had a 3.18 ERA through 34 innings pitched last October, and played a key role in the Dodgers’ World Series run.
He’ll look to do the same this year, as he aims to put together a healthy start in his final appearance of the regular season on Saturday. Before then, though, the Dodgers have a three-game series against the San Diego Padres as they try to secure their spot as the second seed in the NL. The first game of that series comes Tuesday at 7:10 p.m. PT.

That is the first day he's eligible to return. “Unless I hear otherwise," Roberts said before Tuesday's series opener against the Padres, "he’ll be in the lineup tomorrow.” With Ohtani being activated on Wednesday, he will have five regular-season games to get up to speed before the postseason. Roberts said recently he expects O
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced that Shohei Ohtani will be activated off the 15-day injured list before Wednesday's game against the San Diego Padres.
That is the first day he's eligible to return.
“Unless I hear otherwise," Roberts said before Tuesday's series opener against the Padres, "he’ll be in the lineup tomorrow.”
With Ohtani being activated on Wednesday, he will have five regular-season games to get up to speed before the postseason. Roberts said recently he expects Ohtani to play every day as he ramps up to being ready for October.
“Absolutely," Roberts said. "He’ll need those live at-bats."
Roberts said Ohtani is "considerably better" than he was before the IL stint, adding "if he was a 5 [out of 10] before, he's probably an 8 or 9 now."
Over the weekend, the manager discussed how Ohtani would likely have to play through discomfort for the remainder of the season.
“I think there’s a difference between discomfort and pain. Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes," Roberts said.
“Honestly I think that’s just a better question for Shohei to give more specifics, but I do think that when he’s activated it’s going to be the best physical place he’s been in in quite some time.”
Dave Roberts Still Weighing Batting Order With Shohei Ohtani Returning
While Ohtani has consistently hit leadoff for the Dodgers since midway through the 2024 season, Roberts said he's still deciding how his lineup will look.
Mookie Betts' recent surge has him as a candidate to remain in the leadoff spot. Roberts said it could come down to matchups, meaning Ohtani would lead off against right-handers and Betts would lead off against lefties.
In that situation, Ohtani would likely hit second behind Betts against lefties.
If Ohtani looks like himself out the gate, though, he could overtake Betts as the everyday leadoff hitter.
Dave Roberts Announces Blake Snell's Next Start
In addition to Ohtani, Roberts had good news on Snell, who threw a bullpen session on Tuesday and is expected to pitch on Saturday against the San Francisco Giants in his final start of the regular season.
Snell exited his last start on Sept. 16 after one inning due to groin tightness, and there was immediate concern about his status moving forward.
However, Snell has progressed well, and is now lined up to start the penultimate game of the regular season before likely pitching Game 3 of the Dodgers' first postseason series behind Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto.

item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list.
Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger.
Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
Pages was an All-Star starter this season, and when he got hurt was tied with Yoshinobu Yamamoto for second-highest FanGraphs WAR (3.9) on the team, behind only Shohei Ohtani. By Baseball Reference WAR, Pages is still third on the team now at 5.4, trailing only Ohtani and Yamamoto. That’ll happen with a .272/.338/.458 batting line with a 118 wRC+ combined with plus-defense in center field.
Before getting hit by an errant fastball on August 21, Pages started 125 of the Dodgers’ 129 games, and led the team in plate appearances (550) at the time. Pages and Ohtani are still tied for the Dodgers’ lead with 80 runs batted in. With Pages out, Alek Thomas was first called up to start six games in center field, followed by Tommy Edman starting 17 games, plus three starts by Alex Call and one by Kiké Hernández.
With Edman moving to the outfield and once Thomas was optioned, Miguel Rojas (10) and Alex Freeland (eight) have covered all but one of the starts at second base in September.
Sasaki struggled earlier in the season, but improved as the season progressed. He has a streak of six straight starts with no more than two runs allowed until his blister start in Atlanta. On the season, Sasaki has a 4.46 ERA and 4.42 xERA, but since July 8 he’s down to a 3.25 ERA and 3.76 xERA in eight starts.
With Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Tyler Glasnow set for the postseason rotation, the Dodgers will see over the next two weeks if Blake Snell will be hampered by his left groin discomfort, and will have Sheehan at the ready. That allows them to use Sasaki in relief, as they did last postseason out of necessity.
“I could see multiples [innings], but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings,” manager Dave Roberts said on Sunday.
Last season was a different situation for Sasaki, who struggled mightily as a starter and spend four months on the injured list before returning in the final week of the regular season. There was no room in the rotation, so he pitched in relief in the postseason. He wasn’t dominant — only six strikeouts among his 43 batters faced, with five walks — but he was effective, allowing only one run over nine appearances and 10 2/3 innings, the highlight his perfect three innings of relief in the Dodgers’ NLDS Game 4 clincher over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Sasaki saved three games last postseason. Roberts said Sasaki probably wouldn’t get an opportunity in a save situation right away this week, but it could progress to that by the postseason.
“I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably starting a clean inning,” Roberts said. “He’s done it, he’s really good. He’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff. And you really just need four starters. So we’re in a good spot there, for now.”
Sheehan has been fantastic of late, allowing only one run in three starts for the Dodgers over the previous two weeks, with 24 strikeouts in 17 innings. The plan for Sheehan is to start on Saturday for Oklahoma City should the Comets advance to the Triple-A championship game.
Alfonzo was back with the Dodgers since September 6 when Dalton Rushing was placed on the injured list with elbow soreness. In the 14 games since, Alfonzo played only once, pinch-hitting as the designated hitter at the end of a 14-1 blowout of the Cincinnati Reds. He struck out.
Alfonzo made his major league debut against the Padres on July 5, and started nine games behind the plate. He had five hits in 28 at-bats with three doubles and four runs batted in.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers' Emmet Sheehan Sends Message Amid Postseason Roster Push
item.dc:creator: Aaron Coloma
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan sent a message to the team ahead of the postseason with his role on the team still uncertain. Sheehan went to the minors at the beginning of August following the arrival of Tarik Skubal and a string of poor results on his part. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan sent a message to the team ahead of the postseason with his role on the team still uncertain.
Sheehan went to the minors at the beginning of August following the arrival of Tarik Skubal and a string of poor results on his part. Prior to his stint in the minors, Sheehan had a 5.29 ERA and had just allowed five earned runs in just 2.2 innings pitched.
How Long Was Emmet Sheehan in the Minors?
He managed to get right in the minors, though, allowing just three earned runs over the course of 18 innings pitched in Triple-A. He returned in the middle of September, and has three starts under his belt since returning.
In those appearances, Sheehan has a 0.53 ERA over the course of 17 innings pitched, striking out 24 batters. He pitched Sunday, striking out nine batters through 5.1 scoreless innings of relief, during which he only allowed one hit and one walk. On the year, Sheehan now has a 4.57 ERA through 112.1 innings pitched, striking out 132 batters during his time in MLB.
The Dodgers are optioning him back to Triple-A to keep their bullpen fresh throughout the remainder of the season as they look to secure the No. 2 seed in the NL, but he can still feature in the postseason and is willing to do whatever it takes to help the team.
“I feel like I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan told Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez and reporters. “Whatever role they want me to do going forward, I’m ready to do it. It was nice to get that experience coming out of the pen, and I’m ready to go.”
What Role Would Emmet Sheehan Have in the Postseason?
Sheehan has predominantly played as a starter for the Dodgers this season, making his first relief appearance of the year on Sunday, but would almost definitely stay in the bullpen if he makes the roster come October.
The Dodgers have a four-man rotation planned out already, as Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Skubal are all healthy and likely to be the Dodgers’ starters during the postseason.
Sheehan would fit in the bullpen as a long relief arm, and would likely be the Dodgers’ go-to man in those scenarios.
Landon Knack and Bobby Miller have taken on those responsibilities as of late, but Sheehan’s recent results should qualify him for a spot over both Knack and Miller.
Will the Dodgers Bring Emmet Sheehan to the Postseason?
The Dodgers are allowed a maximum of 13 pitchers on their roster for the postseason, and Sheehan will almost certainly be included in those options due to his ability to pitch out of the bullpen.
Sheehan came out of the bullpen for the Dodgers during last year’s postseason, and while he wasn’t the most effective in that role, his recent surge and experience in that area will be key for LA as they look to win a third consecutive World Series.
The right-hander won’t pitch again for the Dodgers in the regular season due to the minimum 15-day stay in the minors, so unless the Dodgers need to recall him due to an injury, he’ll hope the impression he made during his strong September is enough to warrant a spot on the postseason roster.

item.content:encoded:
守り抜いたローテーション、山本由伸 明日23日パドレス戦で28度目、レギュラーシーズン最後の先発へ MLB随一の安定感、全体トップQS率は驚異的『77.8』
ドジャースの山本由伸投手が、今季レギュラーシーズン最後の先発登板と予想される明日23日のパドレス戦。今季は開幕から先発ローテーションを守りつづけ、チームトップの28度目の先発マウンドに立つこととなります。
山本投手はドジャースのローテーションを担う先発陣では、唯一ここまで離脱することなくプレーし続けてきました。積み上げた先発登板試合数はチームトップの27試合。しかも好調を維持し続け、投げれば好投を披露。その安定感を証明するかのように、MLB全体トップとなる21度のQSを記録しています。そしてMLB自身キャリアハイの14勝を挙げ、防御率は『2.51』でリーグ3位につけています。
またQS率『77.8』でもMLB全体1位。WHIPは『0.87』でジェーコブ・ミジオロウスキー投手に次ぐリーグ2位(MLB全体でも2位)で、並み居る好投手をしのぐ成績をおさめています。
特に驚異的なのは、シーズン終盤にきても直近の2試合では圧巻の内容。10日のレッズ戦では7回1失点3安打でおさえ、16日のレッズ戦では7回無失点1安打と完璧に相手打線を手玉に取りました。
これまで中6～7日で先発ローテーションを守ってきた山本投手にとっては、明日23日のパドレス戦が今季レギュラーシーズン最後の先発マウンドとなる見込み。どんな投球で締めくくるのか注目されます。

item.title: [whittierdailynews.com] Are the Dodgers finding the best version of themselves just in time?

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The energy emanating from the steamroller heading up I-5 on Monday radiated for miles.
Fuel was used to power the buses the San Diego Padres used to make the trip north for a three-game series that starts Tuesday night, but only because they didn’t try adrenaline.
Winners in 13 of their past 14 games, the Padres are poised to accomplish team history over the next few days. Never in their existence have they made the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
San Diego has a magic number of two to clinch a National League wild-card spot, although the Padres intend to run through the finish line with a chance at ascending to the top of the wild-card heap in the NL.
“I feel like the whole team is in a good spot right now,” San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. told the San Diego Union-Tribune on Sunday. “We’re playing really good baseball. We’re checking in when we have to. The entire lineup is in a good spot right now. So when it’s going like that, it’s … a good time.”
The Dodgers already have another NL West title secured (their 13th in the past 14 years), but they also have a magic number of three to clinch a top-two seed in the NL playoffs and a bye into one of the best-of-five Division Series.
“I think it’s going to be a good kind of (playoff) primer,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the upcoming series. “They’re a very talented team. They’re playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I’m looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.”
With the Dodgers on a 14-3 run since Sept. 3, they are on a familiar final month charge toward the playoffs. Second-half lulls in each of the past two seasons have transformed into Septembers when the group has discovered the best version of itself.
Last season, the Dodgers were swept in a three-game series by the Angels in August then opened September with a three-game dud in Pittsburgh. A disastrous loss in Baltimore lit the fire after Yoshinobu Yamamoto lost a no-hitter with two outs in the ninth inning and the Dodgers never recorded another out while losing the game.
The wide-awake Dodgers went 15-5 the rest of the way, stormed through the NL playoffs – going 9-1 against the Cincinnati Reds, Philadelphia Phillies and Milwaukee Brewers – then came out on top in a dramatic seven-game World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Earlier this month, it was a brutal 8-6 loss in 10 innings to the St. Louis Cardinals on Sept. 2 that was the wake-up call. It included a four-strikeout night from Shohei Ohtani, who played just one more game before taking his current spot on the injured list.
Properly motivated, the Dodgers have gone on a tear ever since, but it has come at the expense of teams that were not in playoff contention like the Washington Nationals, Reds, Miami Marlins and San Francisco Giants.
This week marks the Dodgers’ first chance to face a team playing at the peak of its powers since they faced the Boston Red Sox, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves all in a recent 25-game stretch. They flubbed that test by going 1-12 in those games.
Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker and Will Smith all have put a charge into the resurgence, while the arrival of rookie Josue De Paula has given the lineup another hitter who can extend at-bats with a discerning eye, along with Max Muncy.
Betts went 0 for 4 in Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, yet he still is hitting .373 with six home runs, 20 RBIs and a 1.215 OPS in 17 games since the start of September.
Far from content with an offense that has averaged 5.8 runs per game this month, Betts said the Dodgers can do even more. After all, Andy Pages is set to return Tuesday, while Ohtani could be back later this week.
“Some guys are hitting, some guys are not,” Betts said. “I think that’s the beauty of the lineup. You get a couple guys going, and a couple guys here can carry a team, and you never know. You just never know who’s it going to be, it’s different guys every day.”
Amid a brutal first season with the Dodgers, Tucker has done his part lately by going 15 for 36 (.417) over his past 11 games with five home runs and 11 RBIs. He was limited to coming off the bench on Sunday after he fouled a ball off his right knee on Saturday.
Tucker was not with the club for last year’s September revival, but he has helped power this one. When it comes to team potential, Tucker is a big-picture guy.
“I think our potential is winning the World Series,” Tucker said. “So (when) we do that, then I can say we reached it. But we feel like we’re in a good spot right now. Our pitching staff’s done a great job all year giving us an opportunity to win every single night. Our defense has played pretty well behind them and then offensively we’ve done a solid job as well.”
“Right now, we got a few guys that are feeling good. A few guys that are banged up. But we’re still out there grinding trying to win as many games as possible before the season ends and just trying to carry it all the way to the playoffs.”
At the very least, confidence will be high this week, in both dugouts.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Michael King, 12-9, 3.03 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.title: [tokyo-sports.co.jp] 【ＭＬＢ】「不振はＷＢＣ」スキーンズに米メディア「苦しい言い訳」と非難「山本由伸は大黒柱であり続けている」 | 東スポWEB
item.dc:creator: 東スポWeb
item.description: パイレーツのポール・スキーンズ投手（２４）の〝激白〟が波紋を呼んでいる。スキーンズはメジャー２年目の昨季、１０勝１０敗、防御率１・９７でサイ・ヤング賞に輝いたが、今季は球速が低下しここまで１０勝１１敗、防御率３・９１とシーズンを通して苦戦。 地元紙「ピッツバーグ・ポスト・ガゼット」のインタビューで不振の一因として「あれ（ＷＢＣ）がある種、根本的な原因だったような気はします」と打ち明けた。 前倒しとなった調整がパフォーマンスに影響したという主張だが、これに米メディア「ファンサイデッド」が異議を唱えた。「この主張は決して荒唐無稽なものではない。ただ、一つ問題がある。もしＷＢＣが本当にＭＬＢの長いシーズンに向けた準備を困難にするものだったとしたら、なぜ他の多くのメジャーリーグのスター選手たちには何の問題も見られなかったのだろうか？ ２０２６年ＷＢＣに出場し、その後のＭＬＢシーズンで大活躍したスター選手は数多くいる」と指摘。ＷＢＣに出場しながら今季も活躍している同じ米国代表のプライス・ハーパー（フィリーズ）、ピート・クローアームストロング（カブス）、日本代表の山本由伸（ドジャーズ）らの名前を挙
item.content:encoded:
パイレーツのポール・スキーンズ投手（２４）の〝激白〟が波紋を呼んでいる。スキーンズはメジャー２年目の昨季、１０勝１０敗、防御率１・９７でサイ・ヤング賞に輝いたが、今季は球速が低下しここまで１０勝１１敗、防御率３・９１とシーズンを通して苦戦。
地元紙「ピッツバーグ・ポスト・ガゼット」のインタビューで不振の一因として「あれ（ＷＢＣ）がある種、根本的な原因だったような気はします」と打ち明けた。
前倒しとなった調整がパフォーマンスに影響したという主張だが、これに米メディア「ファンサイデッド」が異議を唱えた。「この主張は決して荒唐無稽なものではない。ただ、一つ問題がある。もしＷＢＣが本当にＭＬＢの長いシーズンに向けた準備を困難にするものだったとしたら、なぜ他の多くのメジャーリーグのスター選手たちには何の問題も見られなかったのだろうか？ ２０２６年ＷＢＣに出場し、その後のＭＬＢシーズンで大活躍したスター選手は数多くいる」と指摘。ＷＢＣに出場しながら今季も活躍している同じ米国代表のプライス・ハーパー（フィリーズ）、ピート・クローアームストロング（カブス）、日本代表の山本由伸（ドジャーズ）らの名前を挙げ「期待通りの成績を残せなかったＷＢＣ出場者はスキーンズだけではない。しかし、それ以上に多くの選手がＷＢＣに参加した後、メジャーリーグのシーズンが始まると、まさに『いつもの自分』らしいプレーを見せている」と解説した。
「山本は２０２５年にドジャースのワールドシリーズ制覇に貢献しつつ重責を担い、その春のＷＢＣでも日本代表の先発ローテーションの柱として活躍した。それ以降もロサンゼルスの投手陣の『大黒柱』であり続け、何らかの怪我に見舞われなかった数少ない先発投手の一人だ。もしＷＢＣが投手に悪影響を及ぼすものだとしたら、山本が近年背負ってきた負担の大きさを考えれば、その影響が彼に表れていてもおかしくないはずだ」という同メディアはスキーンズの主張を「苦しい言い訳」とバッサリ。「スキーンズは２０２６年の不振を説明するために新たな説を唱えているが、残念ながらその理屈には説得力がない」と切り捨てた。

item.title: [日刊スポーツ] ESPNがポストシーズンの先発ローテランキング掲載 山本由伸、スクバルらのドジャース１位 - ＭＬＢ : 日刊スポーツ
item.description: ESPNは21日（日本時間22日）、ポストシーズンに出場する可能性がある15チームの先発ローテランキングを掲載し、山本由伸投手（27）らを擁するドジャースが1位に選ばれた。 ドジャースの先発陣は山本に加えてスクバル、スネル、グラスノーらで形成され、同メディアは「ドジャースはこの部門で依然としてトップ。現在離脱している大谷翔平が今シーズン中に再び登板する可能性は低いとはいえ、かなりの差がある。以下に挙げる5、6チームのどの投手よりも優れている投手4人を7試合制のシリーズで先発させることができる」と記した。 2位は現在ナ・リーグ勝率1位で、剛腕ミジオロウスキーらを擁するブルワーズ。3位にはフィリーズが入った。日本選手の所属チームでは、吉田正尚のレッドソックスが5位、岡本和真のブルージェイズが6位、今井達也のアストロズが12位、鈴木誠也と今永昇太のカブスが13位、ダルビッシュ有と松井裕樹のパドレスが14位、村上宗隆のホワイトソックスが15位となっている。

item.dc:creator: Full-Count編集部
item.description: 山本由伸でもベッツでもない…ド軍だけ“異変” 球団の顔が…最新格付けに漂う違和感 MLB公式がチームパワーランキングトップ10を発表した MLB公式インスタグラムが21日（日本時間22日）、最新の「チームパワーランキング」トップ10を発表した。各球団を代表する主力選手が画像として並ぶなか、2位に入ったドジャースの“顔”として選出されたのは意外な選手だった。 1位のブルワーズにはジャクソン・チョーリオ外野手とウィリアム・コントレラス捕手、3位のレイズにはジュニオール・カミネロ内野手、4位のブレーブスにはロナルド・アクーニャJr.外野手、6位のカブスにはピート・クロウ＝アームストロング外野手ら、各チームで目覚ましい活躍を見せる中心選手たちが大々的にフィーチャーされた。 そのなかで異彩を放ったのが、2位に位置付けられたドジャースだ。球団の顔として掲載されたのは、大谷翔平投手でも、ムーキー・ベッツ内野手でも、山本由伸投手でもなく、期待の若手であるホスエ・デポーラ外野手だった。 他球団が主力級やチームの看板選手を当然のように並べるなか、大物スターがずらりと揃うドジャースにあって、まだメジャーでの
item.content:encoded:
山本由伸でもベッツでもない…ド軍だけ“異変” 球団の顔が…最新格付けに漂う違和感
MLB公式がチームパワーランキングトップ10を発表した
MLB公式インスタグラムが21日（日本時間22日）、最新の「チームパワーランキング」トップ10を発表した。各球団を代表する主力選手が画像として並ぶなか、2位に入ったドジャースの“顔”として選出されたのは意外な選手だった。
1位のブルワーズにはジャクソン・チョーリオ外野手とウィリアム・コントレラス捕手、3位のレイズにはジュニオール・カミネロ内野手、4位のブレーブスにはロナルド・アクーニャJr.外野手、6位のカブスにはピート・クロウ＝アームストロング外野手ら、各チームで目覚ましい活躍を見せる中心選手たちが大々的にフィーチャーされた。
そのなかで異彩を放ったのが、2位に位置付けられたドジャースだ。球団の顔として掲載されたのは、大谷翔平投手でも、ムーキー・ベッツ内野手でも、山本由伸投手でもなく、期待の若手であるホスエ・デポーラ外野手だった。
他球団が主力級やチームの看板選手を当然のように並べるなか、大物スターがずらりと揃うドジャースにあって、まだメジャーでの実績が極めて少ないデポーラが選ばれたチョイスには、やや違和感を拭えない。
直近の話題性や若手の抜擢という文脈はあるにせよ、圧倒的な存在感を放つスター選手たちを差し置いた画像選定。豪華絢爛なドジャース陣容のなかで浮き彫りとなった“異例の抜擢”は、思わぬ形で注目を集めることとなった。

item.content:encoded:
佐々木朗希の配置転換の裏に潜むド軍の思惑 現実味を帯び始める108億守護神の“ロースター外し”「物事は計画通りに進んでない」
浮かない表情で球団幹部たちを話し込むディアス(C)Getty Images
米球界はMLBのレギュラーシーズンがいよいよ大詰めを迎え、ポストシーズンに向けた編成の動きも活発化しつつある。現地時間9月20日には、ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督は、負傷者リスト（IL）入りしている佐々木朗希を復帰後から救援起用をしていく意向を明らかにした。
今季の佐々木は開幕から23試合すべてで「先発」として投げてきた。しかし、「ポストシーズンに先発は基本的に4人いればいい」と持論を語ったロバーツ監督は、山本由伸、タリク・スクバル、ブレーク・スネル、タイラー・グラスノーを先発ローテーションの軸にする考えを示した。
もっとも、「どんな状況だろうと、ロウキを信頼している」と強調するロバーツ監督をはじめとするドジャース首脳陣の決断には、スター軍団が抱える不安が見え隠れする。それは「絶対的守護神」として君臨するはずだったエドウィン・ディアスのコンディション不良だ。
FAとなった昨オフに3年総額6900万ドル（約108億円＝当時のレート）の大型契約を締結したディアスだったが、開幕直後に右肘の関節遊離体除去手術を受けて離脱。丹念なリハビリを終えて7月9日にようやく復帰を果たすも内容は鳴かず飛ばず。今季ここまで18登板で、防御率10.34、WHIP2.36、被打率.361、与四球率6.32、被OPS1.043とキャリアワーストの水準に落ち込んでいる。

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers playoff roster projection: Could Edwin Díaz, Josue De Paula, even Hyeseong Kim surprise?
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate. They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series. item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers manager Dave Roberts reveals new role for Roki Sasaki
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: Roki Sasaki is among the players expected to rejoin the Los Angeles Dodgers this week as they inch closer to full strength ahead of the postseason. The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since Aug. 27 due to a blister on his right middle finger, but made steady progress throughout his recovery. He has thrown multiple bullpen sessions and live batting practices this month, including 48 pitches over four innings last Wednesday. Sasaki was originally slated to return as a starting pit
item.content:encoded:
Roki Sasaki is among the players expected to rejoin the Los Angeles Dodgers this week as they inch closer to full strength ahead of the postseason.
The right-hander has been on the 15-day injured list since Aug. 27 due to a blister on his right middle finger, but made steady progress throughout his recovery. He has thrown multiple bullpen sessions and live batting practices this month, including 48 pitches over four innings last Wednesday.
Sasaki was originally slated to return as a starting pitcher, but he now appears headed to the bullpen for the remainder of the 2026 season. The 24-year-old is capable of pitching multiple innings as a reliever, but not in the traditional sense of a bulk pitcher.
“I can see multiples, but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings. It won’t be that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s role.
Sasaki won’t be limited to simply providing length out of the bullpen. Roberts also indicated that he would feel comfortable using him in high-leverage situations, but only at the start of a “clean inning.”
As for whether Sasaki could get save opportunities, it’s something that Roberts might consider down the road.
“It won’t be in the ninth the first time, but it potentially could fall out (that way),” the Dodgers skipper said.
Tanner Scott has been the Dodgers’ primary closer in recent weeks, but Edwin Díaz recently returned from the 15-day IL and is hoping to eventually reclaim the role. Edgardo Henriquez also received save opportunities prior to landing on the IL with lower back discomfort.
Roki Sasaki’s postseason success
Sasaki shined as a reliever during the Dodgers’ World Series run last year, pitching to a minuscule 0.84 ERA and 1.03 WHIP with three saves in nine appearances. His previous success on baseball’s biggest stage played a role in the team’s decision to once again move him to the bullpen.
“Yeah. He’s done it, he’s really good, he’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff,” Roberts said. “You really just need four starters, so we’re in a good spot there for now.”
Along with Sasaki, the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen could include other traditional starters such as Justin Wrobleski and Emmet Sheehan. The club’s starting rotation will feature two of the league’s best arms in Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal.

item.content:encoded:
Why Dodgers have MLB's top-ranked playoff rotation even without Shohei Ohtani originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers got some tough news in early July when Shohei Ohtani was taken off the mound and forced into a DH-only role for a while.
With his attempt to return to the mound not going well, he's not expected to pitch again for the Dodgers this season. When he comes back off the IL, he'll slot into the DH role as usual. But the Dodgers' rotation is more than capable without him.
ESPN's Kiley McDaniel ranked the Dodgers' rotation as the best in baseball, even if Ohtani isn't there. The reason why is simple: Los Angeles is stacked with starting pitchers, both in terms of high-end options and depth pieces.
Why Dodgers' rotation is best in MLB for playoffs even without Shohei Ohtani
"Yep, the Dodgers are still tops in this category -- even with the currently injured Shohei Ohtani likely not pitching again this season -- and by a pretty good margin," McDaniel writes. "They could start four arms over a seven-game series that are all better than any one arm on five or six of the teams listed below."
Of all the postseason teams this year, the Dodgers' rotation has four starters who could be those teams' No. 1 starting pitchers.
Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto are the Dodgers' best starters, and they'd likely be the Game 1 and Game 2 starters if the Dodgers could choose who takes the mound.
After those two are Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell, two incredible starters who have a very high ceiling and would be the No. 1 starter for teams like the San Diego Padres, Chicago Cubs, and Chicago White Sox.
That four-man starting rotation is probably more than good enough to consider this Dodgers' rotation the best in baseball. But they also have some incredible depth options.
Justin Wrobleski is an incredible No. 5 starter. Kris Bubic and Emmett Sheehan probably won't start a playoff game for the Dodgers, but they would be capable No. 4 starting pitchers on most playoff teams.
For the Dodgers, those two are likely to be key bullpen arms. That's not to mention Roki Sasaki, who's going to return to the bullpen for the Dodgers in October as they look to win a third straight title.
The Dodgers have eight starting pitching options that could reasonably start a playoff game, and no one would bat an eye. It's an incredibly deep rotation, and that's without factoring in Ohtani. That's how good this rotation is. No other team can compare.

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers temporarily for personal reasons 1 day after start against Giants
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Tarik Skubal has been one of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest additions this season, but the veteran left-hander will now step away from the team temporarily. The Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list Sunday, one day after he started against the San Francisco Giants. Manager Dave Roberts announced the move, according to The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya. Skubal is expected to be away from the team for a few days. The Dodgers will adjust their pitching plans while he handles a personal matter.
item.content:encoded:
Tarik Skubal has been one of the Los Angeles Dodgers’ biggest additions this season, but the veteran left-hander will now step away from the team temporarily.
The Dodgers placed Skubal on the bereavement list Sunday, one day after he started against the San Francisco Giants. Manager Dave Roberts announced the move, according to The Athletic’s Fabian Ardaya.
Skubal is expected to be away from the team for a few days. The Dodgers will adjust their pitching plans while he handles a personal matter.
Tarik Skubal leaves Dodgers after Giants start
The timing comes immediately after Skubal’s latest start. He worked five innings against the Giants on Saturday, allowing eight hits, four earned runs and two walks while striking out three.
The Dodgers still won 10-4, with Mookie Betts going 4-for-4 and Will Smith adding a home run. Skubal received the win despite allowing four earned runs in the outing.
The start came during an important stretch for the Dodgers, who are already looking toward their postseason rotation. Skubal has given Los Angeles another frontline option since joining the club from Detroit.
His temporary absence, however, will force the Dodgers to make a short-term adjustment.
Dodgers turn to Emmet Sheehan
Emmet Sheehan is expected to step back into the Dodgers’ pitching plans Sunday. The right-hander provides another option as Los Angeles manages its rotation while Skubal is away.
The Dodgers have enough pitching depth to cover a short absence. Yoshinobu Yamamoto remains in the rotation, while Blake Snell has returned from the injured list.
Los Angeles has also already secured the NL West, giving the club some flexibility with its pitching plans. That could allow the Dodgers to avoid putting extra pressure on Skubal to return immediately.
Still, his availability will matter once the postseason begins. Skubal has been an important part of the Dodgers’ rotation since the trade, and the team will want him ready for October.
For now, the Dodgers will move forward without their ace for the next few days. The focus will be on Skubal’s return timeline and how Los Angeles adjusts its pitching plans in his absence.

item.title: [New York Post] Roki Sasaki to return to Dodgers this week with a twist
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Will Roki Sasaki again be the Dodgers’ closer in the playoffs? The Dodgers have created a pathway to make that possible, as manager Dave Roberts said that Sasaki will be moved into the bullpen when he is activated from the injured list this week. Sasaki has pitched in 23 games this season, every one of them starts. A blister on his pitching hand has sidelined him since Aug. 27, but Roberts said he expected him to be activated during an upcoming three-game series against the Padres that starts on
item.content:encoded:
Will Roki Sasaki again be the Dodgers’ closer in the playoffs?
The Dodgers have created a pathway to make that possible, as manager Dave Roberts said that Sasaki will be moved into the bullpen when he is activated from the injured list this week.
Sasaki has pitched in 23 games this season, every one of them starts. A blister on his pitching hand has sidelined him since Aug. 27, but Roberts said he expected him to be activated during an upcoming three-game series against the Padres that starts on Tuesday.
The Dodgers had refrained from turning Sasaki into a reliever up to this point because of concerns over their starting rotation. Blake Snell departed from his most recent start after one inning because of a tight groin, but the two-time Cy Young Award winner has since not experienced any problems in that area.
The team believes it has four healthy starters in Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow. Emmet Sheehan figures to be the rotation’s new insurance policy, as Sheehan has allowed only one run in 17 innings pitched this month.
Roberts said he doesn’t plan to use Sasaki as a quasi-starter who pitches four or five innings following an opener.
Asked if Sasaki would be used in late-inning, high-leverage situations, Roberts replied, “I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably start a clean inning, but, yeah.”
Could he close?
“It won’t be the ninth inning the first time,” Roberts said.
But Roberts acknowledged there was a chance Sasaki could end up in that role.
Sasaki became the Dodgers’ closer last year by default, as the team didn’t have any other options. He saved three games in the postseason.
His move to the bullpen last year came after he missed 4 ½ months because of shoulder problems. He agreed to try pitching in relief under the condition the Dodgers let him start again the next season.
Sasaki is 5-5 with a 4.70 earned-run average this year, but was 2-0 with a 3.05 ERA in the seven starts he made after the All-Star break.
The Dodgers started this season counting on $69-million free agent addition Edwin Diaz to be their closer, but the three-time All-Star has endured a nightmare of a season that has included two IL stints. In Diaz’s absence, Tanner Scott has served as the team’s primary ninth-inning option and has performed well. However, Scott has posted a 4.97 ERA over his last 14 games.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers Week 26: Back in the postseason saddle again
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants. They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are taking advantage of the schedule in front of them, with 14 wins in 19 September games, including winning the last 10 in a row at home. This week that meant beating the Reds three times in four games in Cincinnati, then returning to Los Angeles to sweep the Giants.
They went with a two-way under the Cincinnati skyline, first clinching a postseason berth on Monday, tying the Atlanta Braves record with 14 straight postseasons, followed by winning their fifth straight National League West title and 13 out of 14 on Thursday.
Entering the final week of the season, the Dodgers can clinch a bye week with a magic number of three over the Braves.
Batter of the week
Kyle Tucker is starting to turn things around at the plate, and followed up an excellent series the previous weekend in Miami with nine hits in 20 at-bats, with three home runs and two doubles, with six walks and just one strikeout.
Honorable mention goes to Mookie Betts, who tied a Dodgers record with three doubles on Saturday, part of a stretch of three consecutive games with at least three hits. Will Smith found his power again with two home runs and a double, and Alex Freeland reached base eight times in 14 trips to the plate, including a home run and a double.
Pitcher of the week
Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched seven scoreless innings with seven strikeouts to beat the Reds on Tuesday, his third straight seven-inning start in September. Yamamoto this season has allowed zero or one run in 14 of his 27 starts.
Honorable mention goes to Justin Wrobleski, who retired all nine batters he faced with three strikeouts while starting Thursday’s division clincher in Cincinnati, and to Landon Knack, who got the win in that game with four scoreless innings in relief. Also to Emmet Sheehan, who continued his strong six-week run with nine strikouts in 5 1/3 scoreless frames on Sunday.
Week 26 results
6-1 record
39 runs scored (5.57 per game)
16 runs allowed (2.29 per game)
.836 pythagorean win percentage
Year to date
96-60 record
780 runs scored (5.00 per game)
587 runs allowed (3.76 per game)
.627 pythagorean win percentage (98-58)
Miscellany
Half a hundred: The Dodgers have won 10 games in a row at home, and Sunday’s win was their 50th win at Dodger Stadium this season. That’s six straight years with 50 wins at home, plus seven straight full seasons dating back to 2019. Since moving into Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers won 50 home games 12 times in 51 full seasons through 2014. But since 2015, they’ve won at least 50 games at home 10 times in 11 full seasons.
A crowded 10-K: Tyler Glasnow beat the Giants on Friday with a strong six innings, including 10 strikeouts. Glasnow is the eighth different Dodgers pitcher with a 10-strikeout game this season, the most in franchise history. No other MLB team this year has more than five such pitchers.
Parliamentary procedure: After making the All-Star team as a starter with the Kansas City Royals in 2025, left-hander Kris Bubic was on the 60-day injured list when the Dodgers acquired him just ahead of the August 3 trade deadline. Now he’s pitching in relief, angling for a spot on the postseason roster. With his appearance on Wednesday, Bubic became the 33rd different Dodgers pitcher used this season. So far, Bubic has four strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings in three appearances. “It’s just funk,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday of Bubic. “It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact. I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out. I like those converted starters, because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
A quirk: The division clincher Thursday in Cincinnati was an 8-2 win, then came four home runs in the eighth inning Friday on the 20th anniversary of the 4+1 Game for another 8-2 triumph. That was the first time in Dodgers history they’ve won consecutive games by an 8-2 score.
Transactions
Monday: The fresh arm express was busy this week, beginning with Emmet Sheehan getting optioned the day after pitching six scoreless innings, in favor of Paul Gervase.
Monday: One day after a rare bad outing, Edgardo Henriquez was placed on the injured list with low back discomfort, ending his regular season and putting his playoff availability in question. Bobby Miller returned from Triple-A.
Wednesday: Trade deadline acquisition Kris Bubic was activated off the 60-day IL to make his Dodgers debut in relief, the team’s 33rd pitcher of the season. Gervase was optioned and Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Thursday: Miller was sent back to Oklahoma City, and Landon Knack was called up to pitch four scoreless innings in relief in the division clincher in Cincinnati.
Sunday: Sheehan got the call back up to the Dodgers, with Tarik Skubal placed on the bereavement list. Kyle Hurt was also called up, with Seth Halvorsen optioned.

item.title: [Yardbarker] 'Wouldn’t Have Won the World Series': Shohei Ohtani’s Impact on Dodgers Runs Deeper Than Expected as Dave Roberts Reveals Why
item.dc:creator: Srijanee Chakraborty
item.description: Dave Roberts manages one of the most star-studded rosters in the league, and the Los Angeles Dodgers play like one. But according to Roberts, their impressive championship success is not shaped by something we can see on a box score. It runs deeper than the analytics and has everything to do with their MVP Shohei Ohtani and ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto. According to the Dodgers manager, Ohtani and Yamamoto brought a level of discipline and intentionality inside the clubhouse that set a benchmark for t
item.content:encoded:
Dave Roberts manages one of the most star-studded rosters in the league, and the Los Angeles Dodgers play like one. But according to Roberts, their impressive championship success is not shaped by something we can see on a box score.
It runs deeper than the analytics and has everything to do with their MVP Shohei Ohtani and ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
According to the Dodgers manager, Ohtani and Yamamoto brought a level of discipline and intentionality inside the clubhouse that set a benchmark for the entire team. It did not go unnoticed by the players.
Roberts recalled on the611podcast that Dodgers veteran Mookie Betts also felt the same.
“Mookie told me a couple of years ago, ‘Doc, we wouldn’t have won the World Series if it wasn’t for Shohei and Yamamoto’. And his point was the discipline that they had every single day,” said Roberts on the podcast.
“How they work with intention every single day, because what that made, it raised the level even higher for our guys. Yamamoto’s day-to-day is three to four hours of intentionality to prepare to throw a bullpen. Shohei is the same way. Roki is getting there, but his culture- that’s what they do.”
The Dodgers signed Ohtani and Yamamoto ahead of the 2024 season.
Ohtani signed the historic 10-year, $700 million contract, while Yamamoto agreed to a massive 12-year, $325 million deal. They proved that every million spent was worth it, as the Dodgers became the World Series champion in 2024 and again in 2025.
Ohtani’s three-homer, 10-strikeout performance in Game 4 of the NLCS, leading to the World Series, is one for the history books. In Game 2 of the 2024 World Series, Ohtani suffered a partial dislocation in his left shoulder while trying to steal a base. But showing incredible toughness, he returned in Game 3 to play against the New York Yankees.
It does not happen without intentionality, and Ohtani’s whole regimen is driven by it. Shotime runs by the clock; from sleeping to bullpen sessions, everything has a fixed schedule. He is Roberts’ “easiest player to manage.”
Last season, Ohtani finished Game 3 of the World Series by reaching base a record-setting 9 times, hitting 2 doubles and 2 homers. The two-way phenom ended the championship batting .333, with 3 homers and 5 RBIs.
Yamamoto was equally impressive.
During the 2024 Fall Classic, Yamamoto threw a one-hit, one-run game, pitching for six innings. In the following edition, he threw in three games and gave up 2 runs to the Toronto Blue Jays, logging a 1.02 ERA.
“When you’re talking about winning 11 games in October, I couldn’t believe more [that] it’s about people, and players you can bet on,” Roberts said on the podcast.
Ohtani and Yamamoto are the players Roberts bet on. Their success is defined by the discipline they rigorously maintain.
When Yamamoto arrived at the Dodgers clubhouse, he brought his own regimen that influenced others.
He relies on flexibility to generate momentum rather than brute strength. Apart from taking bullpen sessions like clockwork, Yamamoto also practices javelin throwing.
He follows a routine designed by his personal trainer and guru, Osamu Yada. Yamamoto also famously keeps a notebook in the dugout to jot down observations from the game. All these habits work together to make him successful.
Roberts also revealed how the presence of these Japanese players influenced the Americans.
“So now, when you get younger players that we have, or even American players that are veterans, they’re like, they’re doing it this intentional, this precise, and that’s the thing that, as a manager, I love,” noted Roberts.
“Because you don’t know where games are gonna go. Games are gonna get hot, and the pressure’s gonna get there. But you have to be able to default to kind of what you know. And that’s what, again, in baseball, can kind of default to doing things the right way.”
And to the Dodgers’ credit, they did not try to ignore the vastly unfamiliar culture. Rather, they chose to learn from it. Perhaps that mentality is what makes them champions.
